literal_meaning: ঘুঘু দেখেছ কিন্তু ফাঁদ দেখোনি (you've seen the dove but haven't seen the trap)
figurative_meaning_en: threatening to put in danger or peril
similar_in_english: You've seen the bait but not the hook
All that glitters is not gold
example_sentences_in_bangla: সে আমাকে ঘুঘু দেখেছ ফাঁদ দেখোনি বলে ভয় দেখাতে চাইল।
প্রতিবেশী ঘুঘু দেখেছ ফাঁদ দেখোনি ধরনের কথা বলে আমাদের তিরস্কার করল।
example_sentences_in_english: He tried to scare me by saying 'You've seen the dove but not the trap.'
The neighbor rebuked us with words like 'You've seen the dove but not the trap.'
history: This idiom originates from traditional bird-catching practices in rural Bengal, where hunters lure doves with bait while concealing traps, symbolizing hidden dangers in seemingly harmless situations.
note: The idiom emphasizes unforeseen perils, often used in interpersonal conflicts to warn of consequences.
